breeding.method: cubing / repeated backcrossing to Princess

history.text: Brothers Grimm Seeds records that MrSoul found seeds in a Jack Herer bud bought in Amsterdam in 1996 and selected a female called Princess. He began a cubing process using Princess and a Shiva Skunk male, then repeatedly backcrossed successive P.50, P.75, P.88 and P.94 generations to Princess; crossing P.94 to Princess yielded Cinderella 99. The current official cultivar page states that Cinderella 99 debuted in 1999.
history.note: History preserves the breeder's documented cubing sequence without treating the intermediate P-generation labels as independent cultivars or inferring an unsupported numeric Sativa/Indica ratio.

origin.note: The official history establishes the 1996 Amsterdam discovery of the seed that produced Princess, but that event alone is not promoted into a single geographic-origin claim for the finished Cinderella 99 cultivar.

history.text: Archive Seed Bank identifies itself as the original creator of Do-Si-Dos. In a 2017 direct interview, founder Fletcher Watson said he received the OGKB cut from NorCal ICMag in late 2012 or early 2013, then crossed that clone to his Face Off OG male; Archive initially released only a few seed packs and also passed cuts back to NorCal ICMag, who released more clones to the Bay Area grow community. High Times featured Do-Si-Dos in its 2016 Top 10 Strains list, and Leafly named Dosidos its 2021 Strain of the Year. Leafly separately states Fletch bred and selected Dosidos in 2012, which does not cleanly align with Watson's later direct timing for receiving OGKB; CSW therefore does not assert one exact breeding or release year.
history.note: Creation, selection, early seed release, clone circulation and later recognition are kept separate. Later Archive numbered selections/lines and third-party reproductions are not merged into the root identity.

origin.text: Archive Seed Bank and founder Fletcher Watson are the creator/breeder context for the root Do-Si-Dos line. origin.note: Breeder organizational location, source-cut provenance and later clone distribution are not collapsed into a single creation-site claim.

history.text: Serious Seeds says Simon bred Kali Mist in 1993, it appeared in the cannabis scene in 1994, and the line was revised in the late 1990s after the prior male parent was lost. The more sativa-dominant recomposed version was prepared for the next millennium; Serious Seeds records first place in the 2000 High Times Cannabis Cup sativa category and first place at the 2012 Cannabis Champions Cup in Barcelona.
history.note: Breeder-published chronology is retained. history.text: DEO Farms describes F2'ing OZ Kush into Pink Guava, then crossing Pink Guava to Sunset Sherbert to create the Rainbow Sherbert line. DEO popped about 120 Rainbow Sherbert seeds, while Wizard Trees held the same original seed stock and selected #54 and #11. By 2021 LA Weekly was describing RS11's Los Angeles drop through a DEO Farms, Wizard Trees and Doja Pak collaboration. Leafly later named RS-11 a 2023 Strain of the Year runner-up. Current specialist usage includes RS11, RS-11, Rainbow Sherbert #11 and the alternate spelling Rainbow Sherbet #11; later seed reproductions, backcrosses, S1/Auto products and RS-line siblings remain separate identities.

history.text: Mr. Sherbinski describes Sunset Sherbert as arising when a male Pink Panties seedling accidentally pollinated a room of Girl Scout Cookies, with the resulting seeds becoming Sherbert. Leafly places the event in San Francisco's Sunset District around 2012 and records the creator naming it Sunset Sherbert. In 2016, High Times listed “Sunset Sherbet” as 1st Place Best Hybrid Flower from Greenwolf LA and Jungleboys, establishing that the no-r spelling was already in documented industry use for the same cultivar.
history.note: CSW therefore uses Sunset Sherbert as the canonical creator spelling, retains Sunset Sherbet as a historical alternate spelling/search alias, and does not treat the spelling difference as a separate genotype. Sherbet alone and Sherbert OG are not promoted as formal aliases from the current primary/direct evidence. S1, BX, Auto and breeder-specific reproductions remain separate identities.

origin.text: Amsterdam, Netherlands — White Widow's documented public rise is tied to the mid-1990s Dutch seed/coffeeshop scene and its 1995 HTCC wins.
origin.note: This is a public-release and historical-context origin statement, not a claim that the biological cross was unquestionably first created in Amsterdam. The earlier Ingemar and Shantibaba creator accounts remain disputed.

history.text: White Widow became a major Amsterdam cultivar in the mid-1990s and Green House records first-place HTCC results for White Widow in 1995, including the Bio category. The creator story remains unresolved. Mr. Nice officially attributes the original White Widow to Shantibaba and describes Black Widow as the successor name carrying the original parents after those genetics moved to Mr. Nice. A Green House historical account preserved by SeedFinder instead attributes pre-Green-House White Widow work to Ingemar, says it was known as Arnhem's Wonder, and says Arjan acquired male and female plants around 1992 before crossing them in 1994. CSW records both accounts without selecting a winner.
history.note: Black Widow is not stored as a White Widow alias and is not merged with this root object. Arnhem's Wonder is also not promoted to a formal alias because its equivalence depends on the disputed Ingemar account. White Widow Auto, White Widow Automatic, CBD Auto and breeder-specific later reproductions remain separate identities.

808-genetics-ogkb-gsc.title: OG KushBreath Cut Girl Scout Cookies
808-genetics-ogkb-gsc.note: Current specialist/breeder cultivar page discussing a claimed verified OGKB cut. It directly describes OGKB as a cut of Girl Scout Cookies, explains the OG KushBreath naming/public-forum history, and provides cultivar-specific aroma, plant and flowering observations. The page also speculates about the hidden GSC F1 parent and explicitly labels that idea a guess; CSW excludes that speculation and does not treat 808 Genetics as the OGKB originator.

ace-seeds-about-2026.title: About us
ace-seeds-about-2026.note: Current ACE Seeds official About page. It states that the first catalogue in 2005 consisted of regular seeds and names Bangi Haze, Congo, Panama, Orient Express, Nepal Jam and Tikal among those early classics; states that in 2008 ACE Seeds began a hybridization project with Hmong Thai and selected landrace sativa mothers, naming Golden Tiger (Thai/Malawi) among the resulting lines; states that ACE Seeds began collaborating with Yo Sammy in 2019, with early results including Killer A5 Haze and Super Malawi Haze; states that New Caledonia was unveiled in 2021; and states that in 2022 ACE Seeds unveiled an old pure Thai from Chiang Mai while advancing its A5 Haze projects. This shared source record is used only for chronology it explicitly states and does not create cultivar lineage or chemistry evidence.

ace-seeds-about.title: About Us
ace-seeds-about.note: ACE Seeds公式沿革・entity確認。2012年のMalawi導入とACE Seedsのbreeder / seed company確認に使用。

ace-seeds-african-gas.title: African Gas Feminized
ace-seeds-african-gas.note: FULL RE-AUDIT 2026-09-07: ACE Seeds current English and Spanish African Gas cultivar pages were rechecked from identity through presentation scope. Both localizations materially agree on POLY HYBRID identity, 60% sativa / 40% indica, Bangi Haze (F8) x A5 Haze by Neville (Northern Lights #5/HazeA), phenotype-partitioned Bouquet, palate wording, qualitative terpene profile, structure, and listed THC 19.19-22.13%, CBD 0.40-0.45%, CBG 0.28-2.17%. No material localization contradiction was found. The first-party page exposes two cannabinoid-analysis images and two terpene-analysis images, but CSW could not directly verify issuer, sample/report identifiers, report lineage, analytical method, or raw result tables from those image artifacts, so the numeric chemistry remains originator source-declared rather than analytical evidence. The current official cultivar page does not establish a bounded creation location or an absolute release date, so origin and history remain intentionally unknown. Official morphology/structure wording is admissible source evidence, but formal morphology remains outside cultivar storage while MORPHOLOGY_FORMALIZATION_GATE_V1 is active; the existing AI-generated visual remains constrained to supported morphology rather than storing an ad-hoc morphology claim.

ace-seeds-bangi-haze.title: Bangi Haze Regular
ace-seeds-bangi-haze.note: Current ACE Seeds Bangi Haze Regular page verified for Type F8 STABILIZED HYBRID, explicit 70% sativa / 30% indica ratio, F8 stabilized Congolese/Nepalese genetics, structure, Bouquet, qualitative terpene profile, Galicia development/stabilization context, THC 15-20%, CBD Null and CBG 0.4-2%. The page embeds cannabinoid/terpene analysis images and links to a Phylos genotype report, but issuer/sample/report lineage and the external genotype artifact were not directly verified in this audit; numeric chemistry therefore remains originator source-declared rather than analytical, and no formal genomic field is created under GENOMIC_EVIDENCE_FORMALIZATION_GATE_V1.

ace-seeds-c5-haze-x-kali-china.title: C5 Haze x Kali China Feminized
ace-seeds-c5-haze-x-kali-china.note: ACE Seeds official C5 Haze x Kali China Feminized page. The page embeds cannabinoid- and terpene-analysis images, but this audit did not directly verify an issuer/sample/report lineage for those images; the numeric cannabinoid fields are therefore treated only as originator source declarations, not analytical measurements.

ace-seeds-cbd-1.title: CBD #1 Feminized
ace-seeds-cbd-1.note: ACE Seeds current official CBD #1 Feminized page. In Bouquet, this English localization ends with blackberry and strawberry while the Spanish localization ends with mora y frambuesa (blackberry and raspberry).

ace-seeds-congo.title: Congo Regular
ace-seeds-congo.note: Current ACE Seeds Spanish Congo Regular page. It directly states F1 type, 70% sativa / 30% indica, THC 15%, CBD 0.15%, CBG 2.34%, the three named genetic contributors, cultivar structure, and that the terpene profile has not yet been analyzed. Its Bouquet ends with mora y frambuesa (blackberry and raspberry), while the current English localization ends with blackberry and strawberry. The localized pages are one originator evidence origin, not independent confirmations.

ace-seeds-erdpurt.title: ErdPurt Regular Seeds
ace-seeds-erdpurt.note: First-party ACE Seeds ErdPurt cultivar page. Used for identity, lineage, classification, origin/history, aroma, qualitative terpene presence and morphology. Breeder-page cannabinoid numbers are not promoted as analytical formal evidence.

ace-seeds-ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Regular
ace-seeds-ethiopia.note: ACE Seeds current Ethiopia Regular page. It directly supports the P3 / third-generation pure Ethiopian identity, 100% sativa one-sided ratio, morphology, bouquet, named qualitative terpene profile, origin, THC 6-12%, CBD below 0.05%, CBG 0.6% and THCV 2%. The page also links cannabinoid and terpene analysis images, but those report artifacts were not independently recovered with exact report/sample lineage in this re-audit.

ace-seeds-golden-tiger.title: Golden Tiger
ace-seeds-golden-tiger.note: ACE Seeds official Golden Tiger Regular page. The current page identifies Golden Tiger as an F3 semi-stabilized 100% sativa hybrid containing Koh Chang Thai, Hmong Thai, Old Malawi Killer and a 3rd-generation Malawi male; it publishes THC 25-30%, CBD up to 0.5% and CBG up to 1.1%, a bounded Bouquet, and a qualitative terpene profile. The embedded cannabinoid/terpene analysis images were not independently verified here for issuer, sample identity, report lineage or analytical method.

ace-seeds-guawi.title: Guawi Feminized
ace-seeds-guawi.note: ACE Seeds current Guawi Feminized page confirms F1 identity, Old Malawi Killer x Tikal F5 lineage, explicit 85% sativa / 15% indica ratio, THC 19-23%, CBD below 0.05%, CBG 0.5%, cultivar bouquet and structure. The page explicitly states that the terpene profile has not yet been analyzed; no named terpene compounds are inferred from bouquet wording.

ace-seeds-honduras.title: Honduras Regular
ace-seeds-honduras.note: ACE Seeds official Honduras Regular page. The current page describes a Central American pure sativa from Honduras that the ACE team preserved in 2015, labels the line LANDRACE STRAIN (P2), states 100% sativa, publishes THC 11-18%, CBD up to 0.06% and CBG up to 1%, gives a bounded Bouquet, and publishes a qualitative terpene profile. Embedded cannabinoid/terpene analysis images and the linked genotype report were not independently verified here for issuer, sample identity, report lineage or analytical method, so the cannabinoid numerics remain originator source declarations rather than analytical measurements.

ace-seeds-killer-a5-haze.title: Killer A5 Haze Regular
ace-seeds-killer-a5-haze.note: Current ACE Seeds official Killer A5 Haze Regular page. It directly states the A5 Haze by Neville (Northern Lights #5/Haze A) × Malawi Killer genetics, 80% sativa / 20% indica ratio, cultivar-level Bouquet, named phenotype-specific aroma descriptions, qualitative terpene profile, THC 23-30%, CBD Null, CBG 0.3%, and credits Karma with rescuing the A5 Haze mother for the project. Cannabinoid numbers remain originator source declarations unless a directly verified analytical artifact establishes issuer, sample and report lineage.

ace-seeds-lebanese.title: Lebanese Regular
ace-seeds-lebanese.note: ACE Seeds current Lebanese Regular page confirms P4 / 4th-generation pure Lebanese sativa identity, 100% sativa one-sided ratio, morphology, phase-bounded bouquet wording, relative terpene profile, origin, THC 0.5-8%, CBD 6-16% and CBG below 0.2%. The page links cannabinoid and terpene analysis images, but exact analytical report/sample artifacts were not independently recovered with issuer, method and artifact lineage during this re-audit.

ace-seeds-malawi.title: Malawi Regular
ace-seeds-malawi.note: ACE Seeds current Malawi Regular page confirms P4 landrace identity, 100% sativa classification, Old Malawi Killer x 3rd generation Malawis, THC 24-27%, CBD 0.08% and CBG 0.4-1%. These cannabinoid numbers are breeder-published values; CSW does not treat them as independently verified analytical measurements. The page also directly supports the oil/wood/lemon baseline aroma, phenotype-dependent sweet carrot/ripe mandarine notes, qualitative terpene profile and Central African Malawi origin.

ace-seeds-nepal-jam.title: Nepal Jam Regular
ace-seeds-nepal-jam.note: Current ACE Seeds official Nepal Jam Regular page. It identifies the cultivar as an F7-F8 stabilized hybrid with genetics (Nepalese/Jamaica '85) x Nepalese and an explicit 60% sativa / 40% indica ratio; publishes THC 14%, CBD 0-0.50% and CBG 0-0.50%; gives a bounded sweet/floral/creamy/caramelized/honey Bouquet and a qualitative terpene profile; and describes a small-medium columnar structure. The page also says genetic analyses show a unique genotype and low genetic variability and points to a complete genotype report at Phylos, but the external report itself was not directly retrieved and verified in this audit, so those genomic statements are not promoted into formal genomic evidence. Embedded cannabinoid and terpene analysis images were likewise not independently verified for issuer, sample identity, report lineage or analytical method.

ace-seeds-new-caledonia.title: New Caledonia Regular
ace-seeds-new-caledonia.note: ACE Seeds current New Caledonia Regular page confirms HEIRLOOM (P2), 2nd-generation pure sativa identity, explicit 100% sativa, THC 15-21%, CBD 0.03-0.05%, CBG 0.7-1.4%, direct structure/morphology, bouquet and relative terpene profile. Linked cannabinoid and terpene analysis images were present but could not be independently recovered as exact report/sample artifacts during this re-audit.

ace-seeds-orient-express.title: Orient Express Regular
ace-seeds-orient-express.note: ACE Seeds current Orient Express Regular page confirms F3 semi-stabilized identity, Vietnam Black sativa x China Yunnan indica, explicit 60% sativa / 40% indica ratio, THC 7.1-16%, CBD 0.15-8.2%, CBG up to 0.35%, structure and a named relative terpene profile. Its Bouquet separates a deep organic rainforest aroma from a dense earthy flavor with floral details; the flavor-attached descriptors are not promoted to Aroma.

ace-seeds-panama.title: Panama Regular
ace-seeds-panama.note: ACE Seeds current Panama Regular page confirms F8-F12 semi-stabilized identity, 100% sativa classification, genetics as a hybrid between 3 Panamanian sativa strains, THC 21.47%, CBD Null and CBG Up to 3%. THC/CBG are breeder-published values rather than independently verified analytical measurements; CBD Null is preserved as not reported and is never converted to 0%. The page also directly states the bouquet hierarchy and qualitative terpene profile.

ace-seeds-rush-of-siam.title: Rush of Siam Feminized
ace-seeds-rush-of-siam.note: ACE Seeds official Rush of Siam cultivar page used for genetics, breeding history, structure, bouquet, named terpene profile, official qualitative terpene strength descriptions, linked analytical report images, and cannabinoid values.

ace-seeds-thai-chiang-mai.title: Thai Regular
ace-seeds-thai-chiang-mai.note: Current exact ACE Seeds Thai Regular page for the Chiang Mai preservation line. It identifies a traditional pure sativa from Chiang Mai, type LANDRACE STRAIN (P3-P5), Regular format, and source-declared 100% sativa; lists THC 10-15%, CBD Null and CBG 0.41%; gives three distinct Bouquet profiles A/B/C rather than one flat aroma list, with the narrative describing the strawberry profile at roughly 5-10% of the population; publishes a relative cultivar-level terpene profile in which beta-myrcene and terpinolene are each approximately one third of the monoterpene profile, the remaining third is divided among beta-pinene, trans-ocimene, alpha-pinene and limonene, and beta-caryophyllene is the only listed sesquiterpene; and provides cultivar-level Structure text describing a generally tall, slender tropical sativa with pale narrow leaves, thin flexible stems, long internodes and strong lateral branching. Originator-published cannabinoid values are not treated as analytical measurements without a directly verified report artifact. The one-sided 100% sativa statement is not converted by CSW into an inferred 100/0 pair.

ace-seeds-violeta.title: Violeta Regular
ace-seeds-violeta.note: Current exact ACE Seeds Violeta Regular page. It identifies Violeta as a dominant-indica F1 from Purple Malawi x Purple Pakistan Chitral Kush, publishes a 40% sativa / 60% indica ratio, and directly describes a strong robust compact structure with good branching plus intense purple and reddish mature colors. Bouquet wording establishes balsamic as the main aroma with forest fruits as a background note. The current page lists THC 18%, CBD below 0.05% and CBG 0.83%; without a separately recovered exact report artifact these values are retained as originator source declarations rather than analytical measurements. The page also publishes a relative terpene profile: terpinolene 35%, alpha-pinene 19%, limonene 18%, beta-pinene 15%, smaller trans-ocimene/linalool/beta-myrcene, and a sesquiterpene distribution led by beta-caryophyllene followed by guaiol and alpha-humulene. Those relative percentages are not treated as absolute flower concentrations.

ace-seeds-zamaldelica.title: Zamaldelica Regular
ace-seeds-zamaldelica.note: ACE Seeds current Zamaldelica Regular page confirms F3 semi-stabilized hybrid identity, 100% sativa wording, THC 21-23%, CBD 0-0.05%, CBG 0.55-2.03%, Zamal × Malawi/Thai genetics, flat Bouquet descriptors, and a relative terpene profile including terpinolene 23% and beta-myrcene 22%.

acs-og-kush-volatiles-2021.title: Identification of a New Family of Prenylated Volatile Sulfur Compounds in Cannabis Revealed by Comprehensive Two-Dimensional Gas Chromatography
acs-og-kush-volatiles-2021.note: Peer-reviewed volatile-compound study coauthored by Josh Del Rosso. It describes OG Kush as strongly pungent and fuel-like and associates that profile with high beta-myrcene and beta-caryophyllene. Used as corroboration, not as proof that every OG Kush lot shares one fixed terpene profile.

archive-do-si-dos-root.title: Do-Si-Dos
archive-do-si-dos-root.note: Current first-party root cultivar page. Supports canonical display spelling Do-Si-Dos, regular seed form, OGKB × Face Off OG BX1 lineage, and Archive Seed Bank's explicit claim to be the original creator/licensed producer of NorCalICMag's verified OGKB Cookies hybrids. No Aroma, cannabinoid measurement or exact release year is inferred from this page.

archive-face-off-og-bx2.title: Face Off OG BX2
archive-face-off-og-bx2.note: Current Archive first-party page for Face Off OG BX2. It states the BX2 lineage as Face Off OG #4 × Face Off OG BX1, calls BX2 the second backcross to the original mother plant, and gives Archive's first-person history of selecting Face Off OG #4 from seeds found in late-1990s Southern California Face/Off OG Kush flower. CSW uses it to bound the BX1 family/generation context but does not invent a complete BX1 parental formula.

archive-rainbow-belts-2-0.title: Rainbow Belts 2.0
archive-rainbow-belts-2-0.note: First-party boundary source only. Archive explicitly calls Rainbow Belts 2.0 a new regular-seed version of the original feminized Rainbow Belts and gives the distinct lineage Rainbow Belts #20 × Rainbow Belts F1. Its flowering, morphology, flavor and cultivation traits are not imported into the root record.

archive-rainbow-belts-3-0.title: Rainbow Belts 3.0
archive-rainbow-belts-3-0.note: First-party boundary source only. None of those 3.0 traits are generalized back to the root Rainbow Belts record.

archive-rainbow-belts-root.title: Rainbow Belts
archive-rainbow-belts-root.note: Current first-party root cultivar page. Used for canonical spelling Rainbow Belts, Zkittlez × Moonbow #75 lineage, feminized root identity, the MoonBow #75 selection/backcross description, and the bounded sticky-resin morphology statement. The page's mixed sensory marketing language is not converted into category-clean Aroma or terpene measurements.

barneys-farm-acapulco-gold-de.title: Acapulco Gold - Regular (German localization)
barneys-farm-acapulco-gold-de.note: Same Barney's Farm evidence origin as the global Acapulco Gold Regular page; this localization must not count as independent confirmation. It materially agrees on Central American genetics, 70% Sativa / 30% Indica, THC 22%, Acapulco/Mexican landrace framing and morphology, while its structured specification additionally publishes CBD <1% and renders the structured sensory labels differently (Aroma: Erdig, Kiefer, Würzig; Taste: Zitrus, Kaffee, Cremig). barneys-farm-acapulco-gold.title: Acapulco Gold - Regular
barneys-farm-acapulco-gold.note: FULL RE-AUDIT 2026-09-07: current Barney's Farm global Acapulco Gold Regular page rechecked across identity, classification, lineage/provenance, breeding, aroma, flavor, morphology, origin, history and chemistry. It explicitly lists Genetics: Central American, 70% Sativa / 30% Indica, THC 22%, Aroma: Earthy, Pine, Pungent and Sweet, and Taste: Citrus, Coffee, Pine and Woody. Regional/localized Barney's Farm pages were treated as the same evidence origin rather than independent confirmations; materially different localized labels are recorded separately where relevant.

barneys-farm-blue-gelato-41.title: Blue Gelato 41 Strain
barneys-farm-blue-gelato-41.note: Current first-party global cultivar page. barneys-farm-dr-grinspoon-weedworld-2022.title: Barney's Farm Strain Story - The Miraculous Dr. Grinspoon
barneys-farm-dr-grinspoon-weedworld-2022.note: Weed World Magazine掲載記事だが、本文末にWritten and Published by Barney's Farm (Green Body Identity)と明記されたBarney's Farm由来の一次寄り歴史資料。Derryが1980年代のLaos/Thailand滞在中にLaosで遺伝素材を見つけ、種子をNetherlandsへ持ち帰ってselective breedingで品種を育成したという説明、Dr. Lester Grinspoonへの命名、2019年の再登場、種子生産の難しさ、90-95日の開花、ビーズ状の花形態を確認。これは親品種名を開示する資料ではないためparentageの確定には使用しない。

barneys-farm-dr-grinspoon.title: Dr Grinspoon Strain
barneys-farm-dr-grinspoon.note: Barney's Farm現行Dr Grinspoon品種ページ。Heirloom Sativa Strain、100% Sativa、THC 27%、Aroma: Sumac / Lemon / Tangy / Tropical Fruit、Taste: Honey / Pine / Rich / Earthy、90-95日、細長い株姿とビーズ状の花を確認。THC 27%はブリーダー公式のsource-declared値として扱い、分析一次資料による実測値とは扱わない。親品種名は現行ページで開示されていない。

barneys-farm-laughing-buddha.title: Laughing Buddha Strain
barneys-farm-laughing-buddha.note: Current Barney's Farm cultivar page confirms Thai Sativa × Jamaican Hybrid breeding inputs, 80% Sativa / 20% Indica, current THC 24%, explicit Aroma terms Fresh/Sweet/Exotic Fruits plus spicy aroma wording, Cup Winner status, and large/tight/heavy bud morphology. barneys-farm-sour-diesel-current.note: Current first-party Barney's Farm Sour Diesel seed-line page. dna-chocolope-256.note: Current DNA Genetics Chocolope 256 Feminized product page. serious-seeds-ak-47.note: FULL RE-AUDIT 2026-09-07: current Serious Seeds AK-47 page rechecked across identity, classification, breeding, lineage, sensory wording, chemistry, morphology and history. The page identifies AK-47 as an F1 hybrid, mostly sativa, and an embedded Serious Seeds breeder article states that Simon bred it from Colombian, Mexican, Thai and Afghani seed stock, producing a 65:35 sativa/indica hybrid while keeping the exact pedigree secret. The current page's combined Taste and Aroma section describes a spicy base tone with sweet citrus; this wording is retained as combined sensory context rather than split into unsupported aroma-exclusive and flavor-exclusive claims. The page lists THC-CBD levels as 20%-1% and separately labels THC Very High / CBD Low. It also states that an independent laboratory test found 21.5% THC in samples from the 1999 Cannabis Cup, but no original laboratory artifact, issuer, method, report identity or sample lineage was directly verified in this re-audit, so neither the 20%-1% cultivar-page values nor the historical 21.5% sample statement are promoted to analytical measurements. The page says AK-47 was born in 1992 after Simon tested thousands of experimental plants. No bounded geographic creation location is established by this cultivar page.

serious-seeds-bubble-gum.title: Bubble Gum
serious-seeds-bubble-gum.note: Current Serious Seeds Bubble Gum page describes the shared material as developed in Indiana during the 1980s, moved through New England to the Netherlands, and split into separate breeder selections after three female plants were distributed in 1993. Serious Seeds describes its own line as an inbred Sativa/Indica hybrid, dates its release to 1994, says five generations were used to stabilize it, states exact Sativa/Indica percentages cannot be given, and labels THC Very High / CBD Low. These line-specific classification and potency labels are not promoted to generic Bubble Gum.

serious-seeds-history.title: History of Serious Seeds
serious-seeds-history.note: Official Serious Seeds history page. For AK-47 chronology it identifies Simon as the breeder behind Serious Seeds, describes his earlier seed collecting/crossing work, states AK-47 and Chronic won High Times Cannabis Cup prizes in 1994, and states Simon founded Serious Seeds in 1995. For Warlock it attributes the breeding work to Gerrit/Magus Genetics, says Bluebird first entered Warlock in the 1997 High Times Cannabis Cup, describes Gerrit's 1997-1998 seed-line selection, states Warlock was introduced to the market as a commercially available seed strain at the 1998 High Times Cannabis Cup, and records the 2011 transfer of surviving Magus parent plants into Serious Seeds' care. These chronology details are used without silently collapsing differing current-page wording into one date.

serious-seeds-kali-mist.title: Kali Mist Strain
serious-seeds-kali-mist.note: Serious Seeds' current Kali Mist page explicitly labels the current product an F1-hybrid / almost pure Sativa and elsewhere states that Kali Mist nowadays has about 80-90% sativa content. The exact pedigree is not precisely revealed: the breeder describes a pattern involving two sativa-dominant hybrids, confirms major Cambodian and definite Afghani ancestry, and presents Colombian/Thai ancestry only as an assumption. The current cultivar description directly supports a spicy fragrance; that spicy character is also explicitly said to carry into smoke and taste. A sweet-and-spicy scent appears only in an official-hosted test-grow passage and is not elevated to the cultivar baseline. THC is listed as High and CBD as Low without numeric percentages. No named cultivar-specific terpene compound panel or measurement is exposed in the reviewed current page. The current page directly describes a strong clarity effect with an energy boost, recommended vegetative growth of 1-3 weeks, indoor flowering of 10-13 weeks / 70-90 days, indoor yield of 300-500 g/m² and outdoor harvest in late November. Medical-use claims are excluded from effect assertions. Official morphology describes a tall classical Sativa plant with few leaves, dense spiraling resin-rich flower clusters and relatively airy Sativa flower structure. The breeder history places Simon's breeding in 1993, public appearance around 1994, a late-1990s recomposition after loss of the previous male parent, and records 2000 High Times Cannabis Cup Sativa first place plus 2012 Cannabis Champions Cup first place; differing earliest-award wording on the page is not resolved into a single claim.

serious-seeds-serious-happiness.title: Serious Happiness Strain Created by Serious Seeds
serious-seeds-serious-happiness.note: Current first-party Serious Seeds cultivar page. It directly states F1 Sativa/Indica hybrid, AK-47 mother x Warlock father, sweet/fruity aroma with sometimes a little spice, qualitative High THC and Low CBD labels, morphology, naming context, first 2015 IC-420 Cup award and 2016 productivity award. No compound-level terpene analysis is promoted from aroma wording.

serious-seeds-warlock.title: Warlock Strain
serious-seeds-warlock.note: Current Serious Seeds Warlock page directly supports F1 mostly-Indica classification; Skunk plus an unnamed strain from Afghanistan as direct parental context; combined Taste and Aroma wording centered on strong/sweet with acidic and fresh-fruit notes; low/thick growth, large compact flower heads with few small leaves and pistils changing from white to dark pink; headline THC High / CBD Medium; a separate same-page THC/CBD 20%/1% declaration; Magus Genetics provenance; and breeder-reported 1997 introduction/Cup history. The page mentions several terpene profiles but does not name compound-level terpenes, so named compounds are not inferred from this source.

sherbinskis-gelato-33-weedmaps.title: Sherbinskis | Gelato 33 | Live Resin Cartridge | 1g
sherbinskis-gelato-33-weedmaps.note: Current Sherbinskis-branded Gelato 33 product record hosted by Weedmaps. soft-secrets-frisian-duck-outdoor-2016.title: Frisian Duck: Exterior del año 2016
soft-secrets-frisian-duck-outdoor-2016.note: Soft Secrets España directly identifies Dutch Passion's Frisian Duck as its Exterior del Año 2016 selection and explains the award rationale. Under PROJECT_SOURCE_POLICY_V1 this is AWARDING_BODY_OFFICIAL evidence: A ceiling for the award claim and B ceiling for history. It is not used for cannabinoid, terpene, or geographic-origin claims.

soft-secrets-mamiko-gmo-interview.title: El criador de la G.M.O. es trabajador de Soft Secrets
soft-secrets-mamiko-gmo-interview.note: Direct interview with David Mamiko. Mamiko states that SkunkMasterFlex in Michigan selected and propagated the Chem Cookies plant from Mamiko Seeds material received in 2013; Mamiko describes the Chem D cross as first called D-Cookies and later Chem Cookies. He also states that GMO means Genetic Modified Organism and attributes the name choice to contemporaneous Girl Scout cookie GMO-ingredient controversy plus the plant's unusual growth. This directly contradicts the Garlic/Mushroom/Onion name-origin folklore; the latter is not adopted as etymology.

thseeds-bubblegum.title: Bubblegum
thseeds-bubblegum.note: Current T.H.Seeds Bubblegum Feminized page states that its own Bubblegum was first introduced in 1993 as the company's debut release, describes the line as stabilized/inbred and Mostly Indica, and lists sweet berries, floral undertones and classic pink bubblegum candy among its sensory notes. The article also gives a Do-Si-Dos aroma summary. Direct testimony is preserved as such; the article's own circa/place labels are not treated as exact creation-date/site proof.
